one_line: A parenting-expert talking-head Reel, filmed in what looks like a parked car, in which the creator gives three scripted phrases she says to her 3-year-old (during yelling, demanding and restless moments) so he does not grow up 'entitled'.

hook.visual: Close selfie framing of a woman with curly hair in a teal shirt, holding a small foam-covered clip-on microphone near her chest, with a car seat headrest and window light behind her.
hook.on_screen_text: 3 things I say to my 3-year-old so I don’t raise an entitled child (white rounded text card at lower centre, visible 0.0s to about 6s)
hook.first_spoken_line: Okay, so here are three things that I say to my three-year-old son so that he doesn't accidentally grow up to be an entitled child (Whisper transcript, 0.0-6.6s)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it names a parent fear ('entitled child'), promises a short, countable list of exact things to say, and sets a specific age (3), which makes it feel immediately usable. Observed: the claim is on screen from frame 0, in a card, while she is already talking to camera.

beats.observed: Static selfie shot, the white title card sits over her hands and chest, she is already speaking at 0.0s, eyes closed on a downward glance in the first frame.
beats.spoken: Promises three things she says to her three-year-old son so he does not grow up entitled.
beats.on_screen_text: 3 things I say to my 3-year-old so I don’t raise an entitled child

beats.observed: Title card gone; one-word-at-a-time white captions with dark outline appear low-centre over her hand (samples: 'when' 8s, 'yelling,' 10s, 'boundary' 12s, 'feel.”' 20s). She gestures with the mic hand, makes direct eye contact.
beats.spoken: Scenario 1: when he is yelling and upset about a boundary she says it is okay to be frustrated and upset right now, that it will not change her answer, but he can tell her how he feels.

beats.observed: Same framing, captions continue ('“It’s' 26s, 'yelling.' 28s). Calm, soft-eyed delivery, slight head tilts.
beats.spoken: Scenario 2: when he gets demanding she says it is hard to hear him when he is yelling, he can say 'mommy, can I have this', and when he does she says thank you for asking kindly, now I can understand you.

beats.observed: She acts out the child's state: at 40-42s her face scrunches with eyes shut while the captions read 'impatient,' and 'restless,'.
beats.spoken: Scenario 3 setup: when he is impatient and restless, a little all over the place.

beats.observed: Expression resets to a bright, wide-eyed face at 46-48s while the captions read 'ready' and 'body.”'.
beats.spoken: She says: I'll know you're ready when I see a calm body.

beats.observed: Continues talking to camera with the same framing; captions at 50-56s read 'slow', 'model', 'some', 'illustrate'. No end card or sign-off is visible in sampled frames.
beats.spoken: She then slows her movements down to model what calm looks like and takes deep breaths to illustrate what she is looking for. The transcript ends on that sentence with no spoken wrap-up or CTA.

payoff: The viewer gets the three ready-to-use phrases progressively: the first by about 20s ('it's okay to be frustrated... that's not gonna change my answer'), the second by about 33s, and the third plus the modelling tip by about 57s. Value is delivered continuously rather than held to a single end reveal.
cta: Caption only: comment YES if this is similar to how you speak to your little ones, and ask any questions. No spoken or on-screen CTA in the transcript or sampled frames.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: save-and-reuse value (exact sentences to copy word for word), and the 'comment YES' prompt in the caption. 164 comments on 200,709 views is a low comment rate, while 9,185 likes (4.58%) suggests saves and likes were the main response.
why_it_worked: 4.58% like rate on 200,709 views is strong and, with only a 2.7x outlier against a 75,103 median, looks like a solid but not viral organic performer.
Hook gives a specific age (3) and a feared outcome (entitled child) and promises exactly three scripts, which makes the 57s runtime feel like a short, bounded list.

Expert voice speaking from her own parenting ('I say to my 3-year-old') mixes authority and relatability, and the acting-out of a restless face at 40-42s adds visual variety in an otherwise static shot.
paid_signal: no: like_rate_pct 4.58 is far above 0.3 and outlier_x is only 2.7, which is consistent with organic reach.

solo_route.how: 1) Barter a free LumeBook for an Israeli child psychologist or parenting guide who will film their own 'three sentences I say to a 3-year-old' video (phone, selfie, one take). 2) Ask for a Hebrew script of three scenarios and the exact phrases; the SMM adds one-word-at-a-time Hebrew captions in CapCut and a title card with the same 'N things I say to my N-year-old so...' structure. 3) Put the LumeBook mention and a 'comment כן / שלחו לחבר' prompt in the caption and pinned comment rather than in the expert's speech. 4) Cut a 15-20s version of the strongest scenario as a second Reel.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert (child psychologist or parenting counsellor) and their consent to be featured; the SMM has no kids, so should not deliver parenting advice herself or invent clinical claims.

lumebook_version.hook_he: 3 משפטים שאני אומרת לילד בן 3 כשהוא צועק, כדי שלא יגדל מפונק
lumebook_version.concept: An expert from the barter pool delivers 3 exact phrases for a 3-year-old's frustration, yelling and impatience, in the same one-take selfie format with Hebrew word-by-word captions. At the end, a short LumeBook card suggests reading a story in which the child hero practises the 'calm body' idea, framed as the expert's own suggestion rather than an outcome claim by LumeBook.

evidence_notes: Observed: title card, mic, car-like background (headrest and window light, so 'in a car' is inferred), word-level captions from about 8s and the facial expressions are from frames sampled every 2s, so cuts, zooms or brief on-screen labels between samples would not be visible; framing looks identical across all 29 frames. Spoken: Whisper English transcript is clean and coherent, but its first line ('he doesn't accidentally grow up to be an entitled child') differs slightly from the on-screen card ('so I don’t raise an entitled child'). Not verified: the creator's credentials (the account name and display name suggest a psychology background, I do not confirm it), whether any sound or music plays, and whether any CTA is spoken after 57.3s. The 'comment YES' CTA comes only from the caption in meta.json.
